reviews.text: [strike]final boss causes heavy stuttering to the point of crashing my computer; after it crashed it didn't save my progress per phase[/strike] [strike]I don't know why beating the act 4 boss's 2nd and 3rd phase caused the game to eat through 16GB of RAM, but it feels a bit disingenuous to have that when the recommended requirements is 4GB and it doesn't seem to be a memory leak[/strike] [b]the day 1 update seems to have fixed this issue. disregard[/b] card packs make the pool feel bloated and ironically make the different pilots and mechs feel insanely samey from run to run since you get like 4 of them when it unlocks and you get 3 per run the modifiers you need to unlock act 4 feel way worse than something like StS since it's basically the equivalent of taking a curse every turn; the fact that it's a random modifier each run makes it feel even more like you're just gambling in the next fest demos you had situations where your build could not clear an initial elite wave without taking doom; this often occurs even in regular waves due to modifiers like reduced initial hand draw and the one where 8 stickbugs are at the bottom of the screen the first 3 difficulties are fine but act 4 apocalypse and above feel way too RNG-dependent especially since you're so reliant on good factory draws

没玩前以为又是一个没活整的尖塔mod，但实际玩起来和尖塔联系不大，比起卡组构筑，本游戏更核心的要素是回合制战术。只要运筹帷幄，10分的卡组也能发挥出30分的战力，由于独特的血量设计，卡牌的设计也无需像尖塔一样鲜明异常地划为了有短期数值的过渡卡与有充足成长的上限卡，卡组构筑的核心思路不再是千篇一律的从过渡到上限而是数值加战术，再加上全体强度都不错的遗物与道中特别关卡的奖励，卡组过渡强度与稳定成型的可能都得到了不错的保障。 内容在同类游戏中算相当丰富的一档，游戏有三种机甲与10位特色迥异的机甲驾驶员，每种机甲的费用机制与作战风格都独具特色，每位驾驶员都有为数众多的专有卡牌与遗物，构筑花样繁多，在可重复游玩性上也下足了功夫，游戏的更新的频率与丰富度也也看得出工作室的用心，上乘的音乐与不错的美术也对得起游戏优异的内容。 总的来讲，这是一款非常优秀且独具匠心的独立游戏，百分制我会给93分的程度，成品对得起售价，也对得起制作组倾注的心血。

StarVaders is an insanely overpriced and overrated mobile app in exile (at least I didn't see it on any of the app stores, that was a surprise to me). It's basically Slay the Spire meets Space Invaders. Plotwise, you control a mech and defeat aliens, but really the plot is kinda thin and bears little relation to the game. The gameplay itself takes place on a five column grid. The Space Invaders are of course heading towards the planet at the top of the grid, and you move your robot around and shoot them. Here's where the Slay the Spire bit comes in... your moves are all cards, and of course you need to get the right card combos to move, shoot the aliens, and then deal with the "additive" spins like aliens with shields and so on... you get the idea. It's amazing how something can be needlessly convoluted yet exceptionally boring all at the same time. There's an overwhelming amount of mediocre Visual Novel/E-book style cutscenes in this game. The developers failed one of the most basic, fundamental requirements of game design.. "Show, don't tell." So you'll spend a huge amount of time not playing the game, but clicking through endless lines of poorly written VN text cutscenes because the developers couldn't work out how to relate their narrative through the game mechanics, and decided instead it would be better to compete with reading a book for your time. We're here to play games, not read through hours of garbage intersituals. Your gaming rig is not a Kindle. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard. While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality. Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals. The game features simple, cartoony 2D graphics, of the type you normally expect to see in low effort mobile apps. 3D graphics programming does require a degree of skill and competence and unfortunately not all developers have the budget or talent to deliver this, despite 3D graphics cards hitting the mainstream in the 1990's. Considering this is being evaluated as a PC game, having the graphics phoned in like this isn't going to result in a high quality, visually impressive game that PC gamers are used to seeing. The controls can't be customised because the game has such a dumbed down, simplified interface that it's just iPhone screen tapping stuff. The fact that the interface is this dumbed down might be seen as a problem in itself, however... this is a fairly shallow experience if you're the kind of gamer that likes to play games with deep, rich control schemes and interaction. You'll get none of that here. This looks and feels like a mobile app, but I wasn't able to find it on the app stores. Maybe it was removed, maybe it was rejected by Apple and Google (they do have more rigorous quality standards than Valve does for Steam, after all). Regardless, for all intents and purposes StarVaders might as well be a mobile app, it has the same limitations and dumbed down qualities. It's impossible to recommend such a game to PC gamers. We don't spend all this money building gaming rigs so we can pretend they're iPhones and play games that might as well be mobile apps. Those technical flaws drag this game well below the minimum quality standards expected of a modern PC game. One of the driving elements of this shovelware game is "achievement spam", that is to say the game features a ridiculously large number of trivial/automatically granted achievements, 100 of them, in fact. It's a damning indictment for this shovelware that people only bought it for easy achievements, and not because it has any serious merit as a real game. So, should you buy this game? Is this one of the best of the 140,000+ games on Steam? StarVaders has the utterly unrealistic price of $25 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games. The quality problems and defects with this game makes the asking price totally unrealistic. It is impossible to recommend this to gamers here on Steam. Because this is the kind of game you can just play for free on mobile phones, it's impossible to recommend anyone should pay money for the same experience on Steam. For comparison, the $25 asking price for this game could get you games like "Mount and Blade 2 Bannerlord", "Hogwarts Legacy" or "Day-Z". Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this. There are over 140,000 games on Steam, not every one of them is a hidden gem. I'm here to try help gamers find the ones that actually matter in that sea of Steam Direct self published mess. If you don't agree with my findings in this review, you should definitely buy it, download it, and play it to see for yourself. I'm happy to have helped you make an informed choice, regardless of the outcome.

I don't get all the positivity in all honesty. Each run is made up of 3 acts, which have an initial 2-card selection screen, 4-5 combat stages (which have 1-3 mission options), a visit to the shop, and then a final boss. The idea is to defeat the enemies before they increase your "Doom" and cause a game-over, while using various movement and attacking cards, and making a deck that synergises well. This is all well and good, until you get to the point that the enemies basically cover the entire screen (like the Act II Slime Boss can) and all the cards you have are "move 2 spaces" and "shoot 1 time in a straight-line", which you're then further limited on by the "Overheat" mechanic and your deck being filled with "Junk" cards when you're hit by an enemy. I get that this is a roguelike and therefore RNG is going to be a huge factor in gameplay, but after failing a few runs due to my deck being garbage and full of "Junk", playing the same initial few levels just became really tedious, really quickly. Yes, there are crystals you can use to re-draw a hand, but they're limited to 3 uses per run unless you farm more of them, and they still don't stop your hand being rubbish cards, which is fantastic when there's 10 enemies on screen dotted all over, which you have no hope of destroying before they start building "Doom" against you. Maybe it's better when you unlock the other mechs or pilots, because the initial starting mech "Gunner" just feels kind of useless (as does Noel as a pilot to be honest). Takes a whole turn to move 4 spaces to the left and shoot a single enemy, which might not even die if shielded, meanwhile the other 10 enemies fire rockets at you, spawn in a bunch of annoyances and all move 1-2 spaces down toward the Doom area. Yes, you can make busted combos, but you'll probably need to fail a few runs to get the level-unlocks to do so, because some of the initial combos you can do are hilariously bad, because the initial attacking cards are so poor. I did a run where I used the "use all attacking cards from the discard pile", only to be sat there for 1-2 minutes watching while the mech shot 1 enemy then just fired straight forward into the void over and over (because the straight-line shooting cards were all I had). I'll probably try and get through Invasion Difficulty with Roxy and Gunner, but I just can't see myself playing much more beyond that. It's already feeling way too samey and repetitive.

+ 1 works really well on gamehub on odin 2 portal and rp6 love this game, awesome mashup of card battler and space invaders. love the different classes, card upgrades, artifacts and cool abilities. the only thing this game and many others suffer from is that while playing through it, you finally get to the point where the cards you get are just starting to work really well together and everything is starting to pop. then all of a sudden you kill the boss and the games over. no option to loop or press on and take this awesome build to new heights. its like 80-90% of the playthrough is the setup and then if your build pops you clean the boss up ez and its over, or you lose and its over. just to start again with nothing and start the tedius set up again. i think the games need to go for longer or have an option to go for longer. like slay the spire, have 3 big bosses and significant upgrades or new cards when you beat each one. like more heat sync to play more cards, maybe draw an extra card each turn. something to vary the the runs a bit more. when i first played this game i could see myself playing for easy 100 - 200 hours. but after playing about 10 hours, i can see its going to be alot less than that, which is such a shame because i really like this game. i pray and hope that the devs add more content to this game, especially considering the price. Basically what would happen if Slay the Spire and Into The Breach had a baby, everyone was afraid it would become a Frankenstein horror, but it ended up being a well adjusted, good looking overachiever. Excellent aesthetics, easily readable UI, and the main selling point is the addictive, nuanced and crunchy gameplay. It simply has the sauce, the juice, the magic, whatever you want to call it, the star quality that makes you want to keep playing. It keeps things similar enough with each mech having a base of cards, and each pilot modifying your starting deck with a unique passive item that hints at their playstyle. The best part of the game is its a lot more freeform with its tactical grid based movement, the game encourages and expects you to combo and build around things from the very start of the game, it has no early boring setup fights, usually one of the genres weaknesses. The entire game is lean in the best way, you spend barely any time in menus, checking things, or fiddling about, its all gas no breaks, pure tactical combat and deckbuilding. There is a bit of story and its delightfully brief while having plenty of personality and humor, definitely not phoned in, but its kept in between runs as a a nice desert after your main course. I think the deckbuilding genre must be somewhat oversaturated, otherwise this games lack of popularity is seriously weird, this should be considered one of the titans of the genre, usually I'd wait to do a more comprehensive review but I simply had to boost its signal a smidge because 2k positive ratings is shockingly low for something of this quality. Strongly recommended at any price, if anything the trailers undersell how good the game is, if it looks even vaguely interesting I'd give it a shot, you won't be disappointed.

I'm a veteran of card strategy games and when I started playing StarVaders, I didn't think I would like it. Most of these games are tight and well balanced, but this one is all over the place. It's an amazing game and might even become my all time favorite strategy game.
The art style was cute and cartoony, the cards were interesting with some obvious opportunities for strategic builds, and the levels started to get legitimately tough the more I played.
